mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer savings (RSAFS) signals both tighter monetary policy and reduced household liquidity, which together depress consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 10% indicates a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST jumps by more than 10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A coincident rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month signals a statistical artifact or data anomaly (e.g., labor force reclassification), which historically has coincided with short-term S&P 500 volatility and negative returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 5% for four consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals stagflation risk, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 5% for 4 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month periods of CPIAUCSL > 5% and flat/declining GDPC1.
